data.summary: The "node" directory is a scenario definition package for provisioning the Node.js runtime inside a generated sandbox/build image. It pairs a declarative TOML manifest (scenario.toml) that declares the scenario id, installer type, always-on flag, and selectable versions with a Dockerfile fragment (fragment.Dockerfile) that performs the actual installation from the official nodejs.org tarball into /usr/local. Together they form a self-contained, generator-driven infrastructure unit that guarantees Node.js is available on the system PATH for downstream consumers such as code-server and the app web-builder.

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Declarative manifest describing the Node.js scenario: id, display name, category, tarball installer, always-on flag, default version, and the list of selectable Node versions. It is the metadata contract consumed by the environment generator/TUI to drive installation and version selection.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines scalar fields id = "node", name = "Node.js", a Chinese description explaining the nodejs.org tarball install into /usr/local and its role as a dependency of code-server and the app web-builder, category = "os", installer = "tarball", always_on = true, and default_version = "22.23.2". Followed by four [[versions]] tables, each providing a label and version string.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the canonical descriptor for the Node.js runtime scenario in an environment-provisioning framework. It marks the scenario as category "os" and always_on = true, meaning Node.js is treated as a mandatory baseline dependency for the generated image rather than an optional add-on. It also enumerates four selectable versions (20.18.0, 22.23.2, 22.11.0, 18.20.4) with 22.23.2 as the default, giving the TUI a stable set of choices to inject into the build.
responsibilities: Declare the scenario identity (id, name, description) for the provisioning framework
Mark the scenario as always_on so it is unconditionally installed
Enumerate selectable Node.js versions and set the default version

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: A Dockerfile fragment that downloads the official Node.js Linux x64 tarball for the templated NODE_VERSION and extracts it into /usr/local, making node/npm/npx available on the system PATH.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains a '>>> scenario: node >>>' marker comment, an ARG NODE_VERSION={{version}}, and a RUN instruction chaining curl -fsSL to download https://nodejs.org/dist/v${NODE_VERSION}/node-v${NODE_VERSION}-linux-x64.tar.xz into /tmp/node.tar.xz followed by tar -xJf with --strip-components=1 extraction into /usr/local (with trailing cleanup indicated by the truncation).
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment is spliced into the generated Dockerfile for the "node" scenario. It takes an ARG NODE_VERSION whose value is injected by the generator from the TUI selection ({{version}} placeholder), then uses curl to fetch the nodejs.org distribution tarball and unpacks it with tar into /usr/local using --strip-components=1. Installing into the system path is a deliberate architectural choice: it avoids the shared aio_workspace volume that masks /root and ensures code-server and the app web-builder can run Node without sourcing any environment script; NodeSource is bypassed because sandbox network policy blocks it.
responsibilities: Accept the templated Node.js version via ARG NODE_VERSION
Download the official nodejs.org linux-x64 tarball for the selected version
Extract the tarball into /usr/local so node/npm land on the system PATH
Avoid the shared workspace volume and blocked NodeSource mirrors
